subject: Life Orientation
source: November 2026 Life Orientation study guide (topics, key facts, common mistakes and exam tips from the 2021-2025 September CAT papers). Physical Education left out by decision.
overview: Grade 12 Life Orientation is examined in one written paper (the September Common Assessment Task): 100 marks, 2 hours 30 minutes. Section A (20 marks, compulsory): multiple choice, one-word terms, short questions and a short source. Section B (40 marks, compulsory): two 20-mark source-based questions that build from 2-mark parts up to a 6-mark part (define, state, explain, discuss, assess, then recommend with a benefit). Section C (40 marks): three 20-mark essay questions, answer any two, in full paragraphs; bullet lists score nothing in Section C. Most questions sit on a short extract or case study. Marking: 1 mark per fact for 'state' and one-word answers; 2 marks for a point plus its reason or result ('explain', 'describe', 'define'); a 4-mark point needs a statement, elaboration, qualification and outcome. 'Evaluate' needs one positive and one negative point, each developed, or it caps at half. 'Define' wants the meaning, never an example. Only the first points asked for are marked. When a question says 'in EACH answer also indicate how...', the linked benefit is its own mark.

tiers.title: Exam topics, heaviest first (share of marks over 2021-2025)

atomic_skills.title: Careers and career choices (32%)
atomic_skills.description: The world of work, labour law, recruitment, entrepreneurship, work ethics and core values. The four labour-law bodies: the LRA (Labour Relations Act) governs trade unions, collective bargaining, strikes and fair dismissal, including dismissal for poor performance and workplace forums; the BCEA (Basic Conditions of Employment Act) sets minimum hours, leave and job contracts, covers probation and bans child labour; the EEA (Employment Equity Act) covers affirmative action and redress and bans unfair discrimination; the CCMA resolves disputes between workers and employers through conciliation, mediation and arbitration. Recruitment is driven by technology and data: recruiters check your digital footprint and personal brand, and candidates must keep upskilling. Work gives income, purpose, identity, structure, social contact and room to grow. An entrepreneur takes risks, innovates, checks viability first, is value-based and learns from failure. Work ethics means following rules and moral principles; core values guide career choices.

error_signatures.description: Naming the wrong Act (dismissal for poor performance falls under the LRA, not the EEA)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Learn each Act by the one job it does and one term it owns. 'State FOUR ways' wants a plain list at 1 mark each; save full sentences for the 4- and 8-mark parts.

atomic_skills.title: Development of the self in society (26%)
atomic_skills.description: Stress, emotional health, relationships and conflict, the life cycle, belief systems, the personal lifestyle plan, harmful substances and human factors causing ill health. Emotional health is being aware of your own and others' feelings and thoughts; it isn't being happy all the time, and it helps you cope with conflict and change. Avoiding conflict stops it being resolved and lets it grow; compromise means both sides give something up, so neither is fully satisfied. Lifestyle diseases are non-communicable diseases linked to how you live: diabetes, heart disease, hypertension, some cancers. A personal lifestyle plan has goals, healthy habits, coping mechanisms, a support system and progress tracking. Definitions the memo accepts: personality is the characteristic pattern of thoughts, feelings and behaviour that makes a person unique; empathy is understanding what another person feels and seeing their point of view; human factors causing ill health are behaviours, choices and social influences that harm your own physical or mental health; ideologies are sets of beliefs that shape how a group sees the world.

error_signatures.description: Vague health answers ('smoking is bad for you') instead of a specific mechanism and result ('smoking reduces oxygen in the blood vessels, which...')

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Open with a clean two-part definition (a guaranteed 2 marks). A 'define' answer is one built sentence, never a list of examples.

atomic_skills.title: Democracy and human rights (18%)
atomic_skills.description: The Bill of Rights, discrimination, xenophobia, nation building and especially the media. The media's role is to inform, educate, expose wrongdoing, give people a voice and hold power to account; its responsibility is to verify facts, avoid bias, protect privacy and avoid hate speech. Freedom of expression is protected but does not cover hate speech, incitement to violence, propaganda for war or advocacy of hatred based on race, religion or ethnicity. Xenophobia is about prejudice and weak enforcement of laws, not nationality. Cyber safety: protect personal information, verify sources, manage your digital footprint, use privacy settings. Print media is credible and needs no data or power, but is slow, costly and reaches fewer people. The digital divide is unequal access to devices, data and connectivity, which deepens inequality. Nation building unites people of different backgrounds into one nation with shared goals. Propaganda is deliberately spreading misleading information for a political cause. Cyberbullying is using technology to harass, threaten or intimidate someone. Investigative journalism uses evidence to expose what powerful people conceal.

error_signatures.description: Treating the media as all good or all bad: Section C usually wants one way it protects rights and one way it can harm them

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: For a human rights violation question, name the right affected first (safe and healthy living, equality, dignity, privacy): that is often the first mark.

atomic_skills.title: Social and environmental responsibility (11%)
atomic_skills.description: Environmental issues, intervention and campaign programmes, community service, safe and healthy living environments, and global crises and disasters. The intervention cycle: identify the issue, plan, implement, then evaluate the impact. An impact study measures the change an intervention actually caused. An environmental intervention targets pollution, waste, water or recycling; a health intervention targets disease risk factors. Three levels of responsibility: the individual (own choices), the community (working together, reporting problems, volunteering) and government (laws, enforcement, services, infrastructure). Making a programme last: funding, community buy-in, a partnership with local government, residents trained to run it, monitoring and adjusting. Community service builds employability skills: teamwork, communication, time management, problem solving, initiative. Online petitioning is fast, reaches many people and keeps a record of signatures. Crises like Covid-19, HIV and TB damage livelihoods and shift the job market; early detection improves recovery, lowers cost and limits spread.

error_signatures.description: Describing the problem when the command word is 'recommend' or 'suggest' (a recommendation is an action someone could take)

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: When the question says 'in EACH answer, also indicate how this can ensure safe and healthy living', write the linked benefit as its own part: two points without benefits cap at four out of six.

atomic_skills.title: Study skills (10%)
atomic_skills.description: Reading questions, planning answers, managing exam anxiety and time, reading skills and exam ethics. Underline the command word and the number of points required first; answer length matches the marks (2 marks is a point plus a reason, 6 marks is three developed points). Skimming is reading fast for the general idea; scanning is searching for one specific detail. Illustrate means show clearly with an example or diagram; identify means name or point out; discuss means develop a point, usually more than one; critically discuss means weigh different views with evidence and reach a judgement without personal bias. Managing anxiety: breathing exercises, start with a question you know, positive self-talk, remember you prepared. Study skills means the ability to take in, retain and recall information and apply strategies to study effectively. Exam ethics means following the rules and moral principles of the exam; Grade 12s sign the NSC Examination Pledge, and even unintentional dishonesty (a phone in a pocket) can invalidate results.

error_signatures.description: Answering 'discuss' as if it said 'name': each point must be carried into a full idea

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: 'Differentiate between X and Y' needs both terms defined and set against each other in the same sentence; defining only one caps at half.
